candidates.cite: by The British Library; No restrictions; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Plan_of_Taunton_Castle_(1897).jpg
candidates.place_reason: 306e audit 2026-10-13: similarity (4 pts, resid 0.0 m, 0.5 m/px, +0.0 deg) - the 4 anchors are a 200-px (100 m) grid ladder, so the fit carries no placement information: it pins the 1280x1461 plate centre (the site point inverse-maps to plate (599,599)) onto the site point. The plate is a genuine plan of THIS castle from Mackenzie, The Castles of England (1897) - the features match the real complex (Great Hall/inner ward, outwork, filled-in moats, Castle Green as the outer bailey, E. gate, Bishop Foxe's school) - but the catalog site point sits ~640 m WEST of the real castle: the real works (51.0158 N, 3.1046 W = E+643 N+55; today the Museum of Somerset in the Great Hall, the crenellated hotel outer ward, the tree-lined moat ring and the Castle Green, on the east bank of the Tone) were verified on modern aerial imagery. The drawn complex (E-205..+190 m) instead sits on the 1842 Wellington Terrace house cluster and the Stepps Water stream - no castle, no moat, no 'Castle' label anywhere in the 800 m site box - and the real castle (E+643) is beyond the plate's east edge (E+340.5). Wrong place, right kind. Document deleted.
